history.summary: ArgoCDDeploy is now a deploy repo on phase/009-P1 (3fc0b7e): chart/ pins argo-cd 10.3.3 exactly, adds the tracked Namespace (sync-wave -1, Prune=false) and the homelab root CA mounted subPath into the repo-server's trust directory, and config/prd/values.yaml carries the register's values (annotation tracking, 2 operation processors, controller polling and jitter off, 4 MiB webhook cap, argocd-server internal with both nginx annotations plus server.insecure). The repo earns its gate: .kubecoder/project.yaml runs tests/build-deps.sh + tests/render-chart.py, a structural parse of the 61-object render, negative-tested; kc project lint and test are both green. Settled: the ApplicationSet half of D6 cannot be done from values (applicationsetcontroller.requeue.after is clamped to a 1s minimum and falls back to 3m), so P3's bullet now carries the generator's requeueAfterSeconds: 0 — and R6's bootstrap namespace-adoption hazard is close-out A1.

The repo, the pin, the register values and the gate are all right, and the gate has teeth — I ran it green and broke it seven ways. But it renders the chart under release name `argocd` while Argo will render it under the Application's name `argocd-prd`, which renames 42 of 61 objects and rewrites the shared argocd-cmd-params-cm to point at Services that do not exist; and nothing declares the argo-helm repository to Argo, so the repo-server's `helm dependency build` fails outright. Either one alone breaks R6's first self-generation.

findings.summary: The chart's object names derive from the Helm release name; Argo renders it as `argocd-prd`, not the gate's `argocd`, renaming 42 of 61 objects and repointing the shared argocd-cmd-params-cm, so the self-managed Application does not adopt the bootstrapped install.

chart/charts/ is gitignored but https://argoproj.github.io/argo-helm is declared to Argo nowhere, and the repo-server only adds the Helm repos Argo has configured — reproduced: `helm dependency build` exits 1 with `no repository definition for https://argoproj.github.io/argo-helm`.
With server.insecure: true the argocd-server Service still publishes port 443 as plain HTTP; harmless for the nginx vhost, a trap for P5's relay target URL.

history.summary: F1 is confirmed and fixed: the gate now renders under release `argocd-prd` — the Application's own name, which Argo uses and which is also the namespace — so the 61 objects, `argocd-cmd-params-cm`'s Service references and every workload's immutable `app.kubernetes.io/instance` selector are the ones the cluster gets. The regression test `check_release_name` takes the name from the rendered Namespace rather than from the constant and fails on the reviewed state (13 assertions); close-out A1's bootstrap command and P5's relay target URLs are corrected in place. F2 is refuted. `kc project lint` and `kc project test` are green on 9264944.

refuted.evidence: The repo-server derives the Helm repository from the chart's own Chart.yaml, not from Argo's configured repositories: getHelmDependencyRepos (v3.5.1 reposerver/repository/repository.go:1175-1208) parses dependencies[].repository and getHelmRepos (:1124-1163) synthesises Repository{Repo: url, Name: sanitizeRepoName(url)} when nothing configured matches — configured repos only attach credentials — and DependencyBuild helm-repo-adds each before `helm dependency build` (util/helm/helm.go:86-106,125). Replayed that exact sequence against this chart with an empty HELM_REPOSITORY_CONFIG and a cold cache: `helm repo add https:--argoproj.github.io-argo-helm https://argoproj.github.io/argo-helm` then `helm dependency build` exits 0 and writes argo-cd-10.3.3.tgz. The reviewer's repro omitted the repo add, which is the step the repo-server does perform and which tests/build-deps.sh:9 mirrors.

history.summary: r1 F1 is genuinely fixed: the gate renders under `argocd-prd` and check_release_name ties workload names and instance selectors to the rendered Namespace — re-mutating RELEASE back to `argocd` produces 13 named failures, and design.md confirms the Application name and namespace are both `argocd-prd` with no releaseName override. No gate was recorded against this commit so I ran it; `kc project test` and `kc project lint` are green. Two advisory defects remain inside the new check — it KeyErrors on a dex-disabled render (the switch P2 owns) and its params/Services cross-check cannot fail for the reason its comment gives — neither blocking.

findings.summary: check_release_name indexes render content a correct render need not carry: with `dex.enabled: false` — the switch plan.md:374 leaves to P2 — the gate dies `KeyError: 'server.dex.server'` on a correct render, and dropping the Namespace template raises StopIteration at :96 before check_namespace_manifest can report the named D25 failure it owns.

The argocd-cmd-params-cm/Services cross-check at :111-121 cannot fail for the release-name mismatch its comment names — both sides derive from the same .Release.Name in one render; under the RELEASE="argocd" mutation 13 assertions fired and this was not one of them, leaving only false-positive outcomes.

findings.summary: The gate compares the hook's per-cluster literals to clusters.yaml's prd values but iterates hard-coded key tuples, so a key added to that file leaves the hook environment short and the gate green (mutation-witnessed).

findings.summary: The relay pod runs as root with the default ServiceAccount token automounted and no securityContext, so a compromise yields more than the HMAC secret the consult's §2 blast radius claims.

check_relay's "only the relay is internet-facing" assertion matches the literal "yes" while nginx-configurator's parse_bool also treats "true" as public, so a second public Service could pass the gate.
The comment justifying the :80 leg says a 443 leg fails on the TLS handshake, but server.insecure makes 443 target the same plain-HTTP port 8080, so it would succeed.

findings.summary: The tree-wide Argo-entry schema check asserts only the local-chart keys, so an upstream entry missing `upstream.repo`/`upstream.version` passes the gate and would fail generation for the whole upstream ApplicationSet.

The new whole-tree config test asserts `namespace == <dir>-<stage>` for every stage directory, contradicting the allowlisted and documented `namespace:` override key, so a correct future config would turn the gate red.
